title: Coupled Resonator Filter - WiFi 6E (6 GHz) for IoT Narrowband Module
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Ahmed Al-Farsi

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Coupled Resonator Filter filter targeting WiFi 6E (6 GHz) for IoT Narrowband Module. The filter is designed on 42° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 3286.1 MHz and bandwidth of 351.2 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the IoT Narrowband Module module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Coupled Resonator Filter
- Frequency Band: WiFi 6E (6 GHz)
- Application: IoT Narrowband Module
- Substrate: 42° YX LiTaO3
- Package: QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)
- Design Tool: Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Coupled Resonator Filter design targeting WiFi 6E (6 GHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       3286.1 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       351.2 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.8 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 9.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 31.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 36.0 dB
Q Factor:               1198
Temperature Coefficient:-23.5 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.6 x 1.7 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   5
Electrode Material:     W
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b and load the Coupled Resonator Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 42° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 3286.1 MHz, BW 351.2 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.8 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, 42° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N5227B PNA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 9858 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.8 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 9.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 527 MHz offset >= 31.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 10 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 9.7 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +28 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 95%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-09-06
Devices Tested:         68
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.45 dB
Return Loss (meas):     11.1 dB
Rejection (meas):       33.6 dB
Isolation (meas):       40.8 dB
Q Factor (meas):        1198
Group Delay Variation:  5.1 ns
Power Handling:         +29 dBm
Die Yield:              97.4%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Coupled Resonator Filter design demonstrated acceptable performance for WiFi 6E (6 GHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Package parasitic effects were consistent with 3D EM model predictions.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
